A common path is: machining apprentice → patternmaking assistant → independent patternmaker → precision patternmaker → mold engineer.

Metal and plastic patternmakers create molds, patterns, and gauges from engineering drawings. They coordinate marking, carving, adjustment, and inspection to ensure the precision and consistency of mass-produced parts.

paragraphs: In the morning, mark and carve metal from drawings and adjust the first pattern for a trial cut. At midday, measure the prototype on a coordinate measuring machine and repair the pattern even for a tiny deviation. In the afternoon, repeat trial cuts to confirm stability and archive gauges and process sheets. Rush orders can require overnight adjustment until a qualified pattern is ready.

In one sentence: turn drawings into molds that support mass reproduction. Duties include drawing interpretation, carving, trial cutting, dimensional measurement, pattern repair, and archiving. The role combines manual and analytical work and forms the first checkpoint for precision.
